# References

- [doi:10.1002/pmic.201100463](https://doi.org/10.1002/pmic.201100463): the iRT concept: a normalized, run-independent retention time scale that a run is mapped onto by a calibration (Escher et al., Proteomics 12:1111, 2012)
- [doi:10.1080/01621459.1979.10481038](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1979.10481038): robust LOWESS with tricube local lines and bisquare reweighting at 6 x the median absolute residual, the curve IrtCalibrationKind.Lowess fits (Cleveland, J Am Stat Assoc 74:829, 1979)

# Not yet verified

The spec lists these as open; they are reported, never hidden:

- The fitted curve cannot be returned: IrtCalibrationModel's knots and end slopes are private fields and its constructor is internal (IrtCalibration.cs:273-278). A public read-only Knots (and the two end slopes) would let the envelope carry each group's curve, at most Knots points, for plotting and for reuse without refitting (PUSH-TO-MAINLAND).
- IrtCalibration.Line, the two-point line a search uses before any anchors exist, is not projected: it is useful only inside a search engine. Revisit on demand.
- Calibrated minutes cannot be written back into a .msl: MslLibrary.WithCalibratedRetentionTimes takes a slope and intercept, and mzLib does not route it through IrtCalibrationModel (mzLib \#1387 says that is a separate PR).
